title: A routine one step at a time
description: Set a sequence with durations, see the current step and change the plan as the day goes on.

blocks.text: A person sets a sequence of actions with approximate durations. While it runs, the current step and the next one are visible; a late start or a step that drags on does not mean putting the whole day together again.

quote.text:
Nothing helps my ADHD time blindness more.
It’s honestly life changing.

blocks.text: At first one repeating routine is enough, along with the option to skip, extend or move a step. A reminder should help you come back, not hide the rest of the plan behind error messages.
A routine has to survive running late

Personal praise from an author with ADHD does not prove that the timer has a therapeutic effect. Usefulness is worth judging on an ordinary routine that goes off course: has it become clearer what to do next, and does the schedule have to be maintained all the time.
